chunk_findings.detail: The baseline format writes raw TAB-separated fields without escaping. A valid POSIX path such as `ddflow/foo\tbar.py` is recorded by `format_baseline` with an embedded tab; `parse_baseline` then does `kind, family, path, n = raw.split("\t")`, receives five fields, and raises `ValueError` (a newline in a path similarly corrupts `splitlines()`). The ratchet therefore cannot round-trip its own baselines for valid filesystem names.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces.py:format_baseline, parse_baseline

chunk_findings.detail: `_git_hooks_join` is invoked for every `ast.Call` and flattens any call's positional arguments, but it never checks that the call is `os.path.join`, `Path`, or any path constructor. Given `logger.debug(".git", "hooks")` or `fake(".git", "hooks")`, the scanner emits a `managed-file` site for `.git/hooks`, although no managed file is referenced. This is a false dependency and can make the arch guard fail on a false positive.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_git_hooks_join

chunk_findings.detail: Managed-file detection runs on every non-prose string literal before URL classification and does not skip URL strings. A literal like `"https://example.com/settings.json"` produces both a `network` site and a `managed-file` site with family `settings.json`. A URL path component is not a local file owned by another tool, so this is a false `managed-file` dependency.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_literal_site

chunk_findings.detail: For shell-invocation strings, only `e.value.split()[0]` is used. Given `os.system("git status && pre-commit run")`, the scanner records only `program` family `git` and misses `pre-commit`, a second external program run by the same command. This underreports interfaces and defeats the “every external interface” census for compound shell commands.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:program_of

chunk_findings.detail: `os.environ["FOO"] += ":x"` is an environment-variable read: augmented assignment invokes `__getitem__` before `__setitem__`. In that AST, the `Subscript` parent has `ctx=ast.Store`, so `_environ` enters its `Subscript` branch but skips recording because it only records when the `ctx` is `ast.Load`. The scanner therefore fails to count this environment read.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_environ

chunk_findings.detail: `file_protocols` is built from every `ast.Constant` method string, including `self.prose` docstrings/bare string statements. A docstring/statement exactly equal to `"tools/list"` will make an unrelated real `"jsonrpc"` literal be recorded as `protocol mcp`, so a docstring can change the emitted site despite the intent that docstrings/string statements cannot produce or influence hits.

chunk_findings.detail: The tab fix is incomplete: `format_baseline` is unchanged and still writes raw TAB-separated fields, while `parse_baseline` reads the baseline with `text.splitlines()`. A POSIX path may contain a newline (or any other `splitlines()` line boundary). If `scan()` records a site for a file named `ddflow/a\nb.py`, `format_baseline` emits `program\tgit\tddflow/a\nb.py\t1`; `parse_baseline` then sees the first physical line `program\tgit\tddflow/a`, attempts `rest.rsplit("\t", 1)`, and raises `ValueError`. The new API ratchet path calls `I.parse_baseline(committed.read_text())` without catching this, so a valid filesystem name can make the interface view fail. The added round-trip test covers an embedded tab but not a line-boundary character, so the earlier “fixed” claim does not cover this case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces.py:parse_baseline (line 136)

chunk_findings.detail: The new URL guard is applied only to the `MANAGED_NAMES` managed-file rule. The separate `.git/hooks` managed-file rule is still executed unconditionally after `_URL.match(v)`. Given the literal `"https://example.com/.git/hooks/pre-commit"`, `_URL.match` succeeds and the scanner records `network host:example.com`, but `"/" + GIT_HOOKS in v` is also true, so it additionally records a local `managed-file` dependency for `.git/hooks`. A URL path component is not a local file owned by another tool, so this is a false interface site and the ratchet can fail on it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_literal_site

chunk_findings.detail: `programs_of` splits shell-string literals on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, and newline without respecting shell quoting or escapes. Given `os.system("git commit -m 'fix && bug'")`, the scanner splits inside the quoted commit message and adds a second program site derived from `bug'` (or `bug` after `_base` strips the quote), even though the shell runs only `git`. The same happens for regex-like arguments such as `grep -E 'a|b'`, where `b'` becomes a program family. This creates arbitrary false program dependencies from ordinary quoted arguments and can make the external-interface ratchet fail on false positives.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:programs_of

chunk_findings.detail: The new top-level guard admits any dotted call ending in `.joinpath`, but the recursive `flat` helper only admits calls whose dotted name is in `_PATH_CTORS`. For input `p.joinpath(".git", p.joinpath("hooks"))`, the outer call passes because `name.endswith(".joinpath")`, but when `flat` processes the second argument it sees an `ast.Call` with dotted name `p.joinpath`, which is not in the fixed `_PATH_CTORS` set, so it appends `None` instead of recursing into the `"hooks"` constant. The flattened fragments for the outer call become `[".git", None]`, not `[".git", "hooks"]`, and the nested call visited separately only contributes `["hooks"]`; therefore no `.git/hooks` managed-file site is emitted. This is a false negative introduced by the path-constructor restriction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_git_hooks_join

chunk_findings.detail: The new test asserts that the scanner must emit **no** interface sites for any file whose module is in `I.SELF_MODULES`, i.e. it enforces a whole-module exclusion, not just exclusion of the scanner’s pattern-table constants. Given a real external interface inside a self module, for example adding `subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], ...)` or `os.environ["DDFLOW_ARCH_BASELINE"]` to `ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py`, `I.scan(ROOT)` will suppress those sites because the module is self-excluded, and this test still passes. The ratchet can therefore report “no grew/shrank” while an external CLI/environment interface in the census module itself is uncounted, defeating the stated goal of proving “every external interface goes through its adapter.” The pattern-table strings should be filtered by node/context, not by excluding all call sites in the module.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_arch_interfaces.py:test_the_census_does_not_count_its_own_pattern_tables

chunk_findings.detail: The previous tab-round-trip issue is only partly fixed. `parse_baseline` now uses `raw.split("\t", 2)` and `rest.rsplit("\t", 1)`, which handles an embedded tab, but the baseline format still writes the path field verbatim and `parse_baseline` still iterates `text.splitlines()`. A valid POSIX path such as `ddflow/foo\nbar.py` is therefore written with a literal newline inside the path; reading that committed baseline splits it into a separate record, and `_interfaces` then raises `ValueError` from `raw.split("\t", 2)` on the path fragment. The added test only round-trips a tab path and does not answer this case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces.py:format_baseline, parse_baseline

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier confirmed finding still holds. This diff adds `_PATH_CTORS` but contains no hunk changing `_git_hooks_join`; the function therefore still does not check that the call is a path constructor before flattening positional arguments. A call such as `fake(".git", "hooks")` still emits a `managed-file` site for `.git/hooks`, and the added conformance test cannot change that runtime behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_git_hooks_join

chunk_findings.detail: `programs_of` now treats every string constant as a shell command string, even for non-shell calls. For `os.execv("/tmp/foo|bar", args)`, the executable basename is `foo|bar`, but `_SHELL_SPLIT.split` cuts at the `|` and records `program foo` instead. The scanner thus reports the wrong family and can miss the real interface. The same splitter also omits `&`, so `os.system("git status & pre-commit run")` records only `git` and misses `pre-commit`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:programs_of

chunk_findings.detail: The branch previously counted `ddflow.infra.proc.replace_process` explicitly; this diff removes that condition and folds the branch into `_SUBPROCESS | _PROC | _EXEC | _SHELL`. That name was not in those sets (otherwise the old explicit condition would have been redundant). A call `ddflow.infra.proc.replace_process(["python", "-m", "http.server"])` now records no `program` dependency, underreporting an external interface the census is meant to capture.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:262

chunk_findings.detail: The URL match now suppresses `MANAGED_NAMES`, but the later `GIT_HOOKS` check is not guarded by `not m`. Input `"https://example.com/repo/.git/hooks"` adds both `network host:example.com` and `managed-file .git/hooks`; the URL path component is not a local managed file, so this is still a false `managed-file` dependency.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_literal_site

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard `if name not in _PATH_CTORS and not name.endswith(".joinpath"): return` still treats any call whose method is named `joinpath` as a path constructor without checking the receiver. Given `not_a_path.joinpath(".git", "hooks")`, `self.dotted(node.func)` returns `"not_a_path.joinpath"`, which satisfies `endswith(".joinpath")`, so the scanner emits a `managed-file` site for `.git/hooks` even though no local path was constructed. The previous probe for the confirmed `HIGH` false positive only covered bare `fake(".git", "hooks")` / `logger.debug(...)` calls, which are now rejected, but it does not cover a non-path object exposing `joinpath`, so the false-dependency class still holds at this new place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:346

chunk_findings.detail: The added regression only hand-parses a line with an embedded TAB in a path (`"env\tX\tddflow/a\tb.py\t2\n"`); it never creates a census containing a NEWLINE in a path and runs `I.format_baseline` then `I.parse_baseline` on it. The previous finding said a newline in a path similarly corrupts `splitlines()`. If `parse_baseline` still uses `splitlines()`, a valid path such as `ddflow/a\nb.py` still corrupts the baseline, but this test remains green. The probe cited as fixing that finding therefore does not answer its newline half, and the delta alone cannot verify that half was fixed in archifaces.py.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_arch_interfaces.py:test_baseline_format_round_trips_and_names_no_values

chunk_findings.detail: The new `if interfaces or baseline:` branch returns an `O.Outcome` from `_interfaces`, but the default import-census path at line 57 still returns the bare string `"\n".join(lines)`. Therefore `archdeps(repo)` returns a `str`, while `archdeps(repo, interfaces="CLI")` returns an `O.Outcome`. Callers written to the function’s declared `-> O.Outcome` contract will get a plain string on the default path and fail with `AttributeError` on `res.ok`/`res.text`; callers of the existing string-returning path will get a non-string whenever `interfaces` is passed. The change should have converted the original tail to `O.ok("archdeps", text="\n".join(lines), rows=rows, unparsed=list(census.unparsed))` rather than introducing a second return type.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/arch_deps.py:57

chunk_findings.detail: `parse_baseline` tries to skip comment lines with `not raw.startswith("#")`, but it checks before stripping leading whitespace. Given a baseline text containing an indented comment line such as `"  # header"`, `raw.strip()` is true yet `raw.startswith("#")` is false, so the code proceeds to `kind, family, path, n = raw.split("\t")`. That line has no tab, so `raw.split("\t")` returns a one-element list and the four-way unpack raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (got 1, expected 4)`. A comment at column 0 is correctly ignored, but an indented comment crashes the entire parser.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces.py:parse_baseline

chunk_findings.detail: `_Scan.run` calls `_git_hooks_join(node)` for every `ast.Call`, and `_git_hooks_join` flattens all call arguments without checking that the callee is actually a path join/construct. For example, `print(".git", "hooks")` leaves `[".git", "hooks"]` and therefore records a `managed-file` `.git/hooks` site. That call does not construct or access `.git/hooks`, so the scan reports a nonexistent interface.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_git_hooks_join

chunk_findings.detail: `self.prose` exempts only `ast.Expr` whose value is a string `Constant`. A standalone f-string statement such as `f"opencode.json"` is an `ast.Expr(ast.JoinedStr)`; its child `Constant(value="opencode.json")` is not in `self.prose`, so `_literal_site` adds `managed-file opencode.json`. This directly contradicts the file's own guarantee that “a string statement can not produce a hit.”

Valid keyword-call forms such as `subprocess.run(args=["git", "status"])`, `os.getenv(key="FOO")`, or `shutil.which(cmd="git")` then report family `<dynamic>` even though the program/env name is statically known. chunk_findings.detail: `test_scan_is_cheap_enough_for_the_suite` is a wall-clock timing assertion with a fixed 15 second threshold. On a slow CI runner, first-run cold page cache, or a host under load, `I.scan(ROOT)` can legitimately take longer than 15 seconds even when the implementation is correct, causing a false failure.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_real_tree_ratchet_against_committed_baseline` is not hermetic: it scans `ROOT` and fails if any extra `.py` file exists in the worktree under `ddflow/`. For example, an untracked scratch file `ddflow/scratch.py` containing `os.getenv("DEBUG")` will be picked up by `I.scan(ROOT)` and make `grew` nonempty, so line 285 fails even though the committed change itself is fine. chunk_findings.detail: `_shell_commands` lists newline as a shell operator in `_SHELL_OPS`, but the shlex configuration used above it never emits newline as a token: [REDACTED] punctuation_chars=True)` with `whitespace_split=True` treats newline as whitespace and skips it. Given `os.system("git status\npre-commit run")`, the token stream is effectively `git`, `status`, `pre-commit`, `run`; `git` sets `fresh=False`, and because no newline operator resets `fresh`, `pre-commit` is not returned. `programs_of` then records only program `git`, missing the second external program run by the same shell command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The shell-operator table treats `&` as a command separator, but shlex with `punctuation_chars=True` tokenizes redirections such as `2>&1` into separate `2`, `>`, `&`, and `1` tokens. Since `>` is not in `_SHELL_OPS` but `&` is, the `&` in `>&` resets `fresh`, and the following `1` is appended as if it were the next command. For `os.system("git status > /dev/null 2>&1")`, the scanner records a bogus `program` site for family `1`, a false external interface that can make the ratchet fail on code that only redirects file descriptors.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py:_shell_commands

chunk_findings.detail: The test is presented as the safety argument for excluding `I.SELF_MODULES` from the interface census, but it only checks static import families. The interface census counts managed-file literals without requiring an import (for example `g = "AGENTS.md"` is counted in `test_managed_files_exclude_prose_and_comments`). If someone adds `open("AGENTS.md").read()` to `ddflow/services/archifaces_scan.py`, the interface census will suppress the resulting site because the module is self-excluded, while `A.scan(ROOT)` gains no `subprocess`, `http`, `shutil`, `clock-env`, `sqlite3`, or `fsio` importer for that module because `open` is a builtin. `test_the_census_modules_import_no_os_family` and `test_the_census_does_not_count_its_own_pattern_tables` therefore still pass even though an external managed-file interface has been hidden from the census.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_arch_interfaces.py:test_the_census_modules_import_no_os_family

chunk_findings.detail: The prose exclusion is broken: `self.prose = {id(n.value) ...}` stores the identity of the string value, but both `file_protocols` and the `ast.Constant` branch test `id(node) not in self.prose`, the identity of the AST node. Those two IDs are never equal. A docstring `"""https://example.com"""` therefore reaches `_literal_site` and emits `network host:example.com`, and a docstring exactly `"tools/list"` still leaks into `file_protocols`. This is previous finding 6 still present, not fixed by the cited probe.

`_SHELL_OPS` contains `"
"`, but `shlex.shlex(..., whitespace_split=True)` consumes newline as whitespace, so `"
"` is never returned as a token. For `os.system("git status
pre-commit run")`, the token list is `["git", "status", "pre-commit", "run"]`; `_shell_commands` returns only `["git"]`, so `pre-commit` is run but not recorded. This underreports a newline-separated external program.

chunk_findings.detail: `shutil.which("git")` is recorded as a `program` site, but `shutil.which` only locates an executable; it does not run it. Given `if shutil.which("git"): ...` with no subprocess call, the scanner emits `program git`, a false dependency that can make the arch guard fail even though no git process is ever run.

chunk_findings.detail: `_git_hooks_join` flattens every `ast.Div` BinOp without requiring a path constructor. Valid code with a user-defined `__truediv__` such as `NonPath() / ".git" / "hooks"` leaves `[None, ".git", "hooks"]`, so `pairwise` finds `(".git", "hooks")` and emits a `managed-file` site for `.git/hooks` although no local path is constructed. This false positive can fail the arch guard.

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `I.scan(ROOT)` completes in under 15 seconds of wall-clock time. This makes the suite fail based on machine load, disk speed, or CI virtualization even when the scanner's performance has not regressed and the change is correct. For example, on a shared or throttled CI worker with a cold page cache, the full-repository parse and scan can exceed 15 s, causing a spurious failure unrelated to scanner behavior.

For `subprocess.run("git status\nls", shell=True)`, the method returns `["git"]` because `git`, `status`, and `ls` become consecutive tokens and no separator resets `fresh`; `ls` is never recorded as a second command, violating the function’s description that it names the first word of every command in a shell line.

chunk_findings.detail: Every line in this committed baseline is a Python/JSON-style list literal (for example `["env", "<all>", "ddflow/api/briefing.py", 1]`) with no tab separators. `ddflow/services/archifaces.py:parse_baseline`, however, parses each non-comment line with `kind, family, path, n = raw.split("\t")`. For line 1, `raw.split("\t")` returns a one-element list, so the four-way unpack raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (got 1, expected 4)`. Any test that loads this committed baseline through `parse_baseline` (the ratchet comparison tests in `tests/test_arch_interfaces.py`) will therefore fail before comparing anything. The baseline format and the parser format are incompatible.
